 Judgment

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the minor petitioner in a road traffic accident that occurred on 14.07.2024 at about 3.30pm.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 14.07.2024 at about 3.30pm, the petitioner was playing in front of Home No.347,
MSR Nagar, 6 th Cross, cautiously with due care on the extreme left side of the said Road.
At that time all of a sudden, a Car bearing No.KL-60-E-6768 came with high speed, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore provided first aid treatment and thereafter admitted as an inpatient from 14.07.2024 to 24.07.2024,
underwent split skin grafting over right lower limb under SA on 16.07.2024 and discharged with advice for regular follow up treatment.

So far the guardian of the petitioner spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards petitioner treatment, nourishment, food etc.,
Due to the said accidental injuries, the petitioner is unable to walk, sit, squat, climb stairs, use Indian type of toilet or do any work as he was doing prior to the accident and suffering from permanent disability.
The injuries caused in the accident are permanent in nature.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, student (LKG).

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Registration No.KL-60-E-6768 and Yeshwanthpura Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the car in Cr.No.0070/2024.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant Samarth Bist vs Ummer P V on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193708712/
2 compensation as prayed in the petition.
4.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this court hence, place ex-parte.

4A. The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement denying the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the 1st respondent in respect of the Car bearing Registration No.KL-60-E-6768.
Further stated that the driver of the car did not possess a valid driving license at the time of accident.
It has specifically denied the involvement of the car in the accident.
The Car bearing Registration No.KL-60-E-6768 did not have a valid RC, permit and FC as on the date of accident.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further stated that the petitioner is a minor, he was playing on the road at the time of accident.
The road is not a playground to play for the children.
There is gross negligence on the part of the parents of the minor petitioner in letting free a minor childe to play on a busy traffic road.

Further denied the age,
occupation, medical expenses etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant.
Accordingly, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are framed for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 14.07.2024 at 3.30pm, due to negligent parking of the Car bearing Reg.No.KL-60-E-6768 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
Issue No.2: Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
Issue No.3: What Order or Award?
6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined his father/natural guardian as PW-1 and got marked Twelve documents as Exs.P1 to P12.
The respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
7. The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by learned counsel for the parties.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decision:
2014 (14) Supreme Court Cases 396: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Ins. Co. Ltd., and Anr.

9.
Issue No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined the Father/natural guardian as PW-1 and got marked Twelve documents as Exs.P1 to P12.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
10. It is the specific case of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the offending car was not holding a valid driving license as on the date of accident.
In this regard the insurer did not examine any witnesses and produced the documents.
11. The petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
He has duly cross examined by the counsel for respondent No.2.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has stated that he has seen the accident and he was on the spot of the accident.
Petitioner was with his Mother as on the time of accident.
Further denied the suggestions made by the counsel for the other side.
12. Before evaluating the evidence of the PW.1, for cost of repetition, it is necessary to reproduce the case of the petitioner.
On 14.07.2024 at about 3.30pm, the petitioner was playing in front of Home No.347, MSR Nagar, 6th Cross, cautiously with due care on the extreme left side of the said Road.
At that time all of a sudden, a Car bearing No.KL-60-E-6768 came with high speed, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

13. Among the documents produced, Exs.P-1 & 2 are the FIR with complaint and Ex.P.6 is the Charge sheet it is mentioned that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of offending car.
The police registered the case against the accused/driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of BNS.
On evaluating the portion of cross examination, it can be easily gathered that the insurer has not seriously disputing the accident.
But the main contention of the insurer that the accident spot was not playing ground.
It is true that the alleged accident place is public road.
However, the rider or driver of two or more wheelers vehicle ought to have taken utmost care and caution, where the residential area are situated.
The police documents are clearly discloses that the accident was occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is undisputed fact that there was delay in the lodging the complaint.
At this juncture, it is beneficial to refer the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of RAVI V/s. BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that "in accident cases, human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.

Delay in lodging the FIR thus,
 cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court Samarth Bist vs Ummer P V on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193708712/
4 finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons

sentences.text: then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim cannot be dismissed merely on that ground although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases.
Delay in lodging the claim should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof."
14. In the light of the Judgment referred to supra in RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The Contents of the complaint clearly depicts that the informant has failed to lodge the complaint immediately as the petitioner was busy in treatment process of his child.
So, the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.

Thus, on an overall consideration of these documents coupled with the evidence of PW-1, it would clearly establish that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KL-60-E-6768.
Therefore, I hold that the accident is caused due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KL- 60-E-6768.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
Therefore, a straight jacket formula cannot be adopted in accepting the rash and negligence on the part of Driver of the insured.
So, the materials on record clearly indicates that the accident has occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2: the claimant/Guardian of the petitioner has produced Wound Certificate as per Ex.P.5.
It shows that the claimant has sustained foot deep grassed abrasions over left foot , avulsion injury exposing tendons bone which is grievous in nature.
To prove the disability, the guardian of the petitioner neither examined the treated Doctor nor any other doctor to assess the disability.

So, I am of the opinion that though the claimant is able to prove that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident but the guardian of the petitioner has failed to prove that his son had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has produced Discharge summary at Ex.P.12.

But the discharge summary has not consist page No.1,
which is contained the date of admission and date of discharge.
But in the medical bills it is shown that date of admission was 14.07.2024 and the date of discharge was 24.07.2024, total 11 days, the petitioner took treatment at Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore.
Considering the Wound Certificate and Discharge summary and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be presumed that the claimant has taken treatment at Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore.
Apart from this the petitioner has also produced medical bills at Ex.P.10 for Rs.53,111/- spent towards his Son's treatment.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondents.
There is no repeated bills.

Therefore, the Samarth Bist vs Ummer P V on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193708712/
5 petitioner is entitled for the said amount.

sentences.text: Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by him, the period in which he has taken treatment as an inpatient also amount spent towards treatment, I am of the firm opinion that awarding a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as global compensation under only one conventional head meets the ends of justice.
In view of, I answer issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.2.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.

The respondent No.2 is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakhs only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.

On deposit of compensation, 50% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner till he attains the age of majority with a liberty to withdraw interest and remaining amount shall be released in the name of the guardian of the petitioner on proper identification through e- payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.

The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/-
fixed.
Draw the award accordingly.
